songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line
It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: Fiery Other One/Death Don't Have No Mercy medley, tight second set
ai_show_review.blurb: The second‑set suite of Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One → Death Don't Have No Mercy blazes with manic intensity. Jerry’s guitar is inspired throughout while Mickey and Bill lock in on drums. Viola Lee Blues adds a scorching blues surge to an already high‑octane performance.
ai_show_review.review:
April 6, 1969 at the Avalon Ballroom captures the Dead at a peak of raw energy and improvisational daring. The highlight of the night is the second‑set medley – Cryptical Envelopment flowing straight into The Other One, looping back through another Cryptical Envelopment, then exploding into Death Don't Have No Mercy. Reviewers describe this sequence as “smoking” and “incendiary,” with Garcia delivering inspired guitar work that never wavers (aside from a brief misfire on the opening Lovelight solo). Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann are “in sync and on fire,” driving the rhythmic engine while Pigpen’s organ on Viola Lee Blues is sweet, hot, and unexpectedly fierce. The first set, though more straightforward, holds its own with solid renditions of Good Morning Little School Girl, Beat It On Down The Line, and a soulful Turn On Your Lovelight. Overall the show feels tight, with only minor hiccups, making it one of the standout Avalon performances of ’69.

The best listening experience comes from the GEMS FM matrix recording (gd1969-04-06.135956.FM.GEMS.Flac16), which preserves the clarity of the broadcast mix and captures both the band’s power and the crowd ambience without drop‑outs. Whether you’re chasing the legendary Other One marathon or just want a vivid snapshot of the Dead’s early psychedelic blaze, this show delivers.

best_recording.reason: Excellent FM matrix broadcast with crystal‑clear mix, strong board clarity and no drop‑outs; captures the standout medley perfectly.

key_highlights: Smoking Other One → Cryptical Envelopment → Death Don't Have No Mercy sequence
Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann locked in, driving the rhythm section
High‑energy second set despite minor solo hiccups

band_performance.Jerry: Exceptionally inspired guitar work throughout, delivering the goods continuously; a few misfires in the first Lovelight solo but otherwise stellar, with a brief two‑minute cut during Viola Lee Blues on one tape.
band_performance.Bob: Vocal delivery is mixed – divisive for some listeners yet solid on tracks like Lovelight and The Other One according to reviewers.
band_performance.Pigpen: Organ work on Viola Lee Blues described as sweet, hot and possibly performed by an unexpected player; adds a bluesy edge to the set.
band_performance.Mickey: In sync and on fire with Bill Kreutzmann during the performance, driving the rhythmic intensity of the medley.
band_performance.Billy: Together with Mickey, provides tight, fiery drumming that underpins the high‑octane second set.
